correctness.rationale: The radical is the algebra of positive-length quiver paths and has dimension 2a+2c+ac+1. Expanding [X,Y] by path length gives exactly two length-two equations and one length-three tensor equation; top-length coordinates are free. When the two central arrow coefficients vanish, the remaining equation MN=0 for an a-by-4 and a 4-by-c matrix is exactly counted by rank summation Z. Otherwise, length-two equations force shared factors and the residual tensor linear map has ranks 0, a, c and a+c-1 on the exhaustive zero/nonzero cases, yielding T with multiplicity \(q^2-1\). The final expression is therefore a full finite-field proof, independent of enumeration; group class numbers follow from counting commuting pairs divided by |1+J|. Exact exhaustive centralizer computations checked q=2,3 small parameters.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Known polynomiality and broad algorithmic computability dominate any claim that the count merely is a polynomial. This result therefore claims only the concise explicit arithmetic law valid simultaneously for every a,c and every prime power q, by a rank-at-most-four compression. No minimality or algorithmic impossibility is claimed.

originality.rationale: The proved theorem is an explicit formula uniform over both unbounded outer arrow multiplicities and all finite fields, for a genuine length-three projective-quiver radical. Hennecart–Perry §4 formulas treat paths of length at most two. Goodwin–Röhrle Theorem 1.2 covers polynomiality of the equivalent four-block parabolic class number, and Pak–Soffer gives general fixed-pattern algorithms; neither inspected source states the rank-four closed expression or derives its all-(a,c) parameter law. A square-zero single-element profile and the published Kronecker commuting count concern different invariants. There is residual risk of an equivalent special formula elsewhere, but published polynomiality and fixed-size computability are not mislabeled as new.
residual_risks: A published special closed formula for these parabolic block sizes may exist outside the primary texts and searches inspected.
Goodwin–Röhrle fully covers polynomiality, so only the concrete parameter-uniform expression is potentially new.
The general pattern-group recurrence may be symbolically reducible to the same expression; no claim that such a reduction is impossible.
No independent mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Hennecart–Perry motivate exact radical commuting-pair counts as a quiver analogue of Higman’s conjecture. This is a natural first longer-path family with unbounded outer parallel arrow multiplicities. The exact universal formula solves a finer arithmetic task than known four-block polynomiality, reducing all family sizes to ranks of a matrix with only four columns, and simultaneously computes the algebra-group class numbers for every characteristic. The a=c=1 instance alone would be known and insufficient; the unrestricted two-parameter formula and structural compression are the valued content.
